slides.title: Normal Anatomy & Physiology
slides.subtitle: System of Focus: Immune / Infectious Disease

blocks.heading: Key Concepts
blocks.html:
• CD4+ T-helper lymphocytes: coordinate immune response
  • Normal CD4 count: 500-1,600 cells/mm³
  • HIV targets CD4 cells via gp120 binding to CCR5/CXCR4
  • Viral replication destroys CD4 cells → immunodeficiency
  • Viral load: number of HIV RNA copies/mL (goal: undetectable)
  • Opportunistic infections occur when CD4 <200 (AIDS defining)

blocks.heading: Normal Values
blocks.html:
• CD4 normal: 500-1,600 cells/mm³
  • CD4 <200 = AIDS (OIs likely)
  • Viral load undetectable: <20-50 copies/mL
  • Window period: 2-4 weeks (4th gen Ag/Ab test)
  • Time to AIDS without treatment: ~10 years

blocks.heading: What the Nurse Must Know
blocks.html:
• U=U: Undetectable = Untransmittable — patient with undetectable VL cannot sexually transmit HIV
  • 4th generation test detects p24 antigen + antibodies — window period 2-4 weeks
  • PEP: Post-exposure prophylaxis within 72 hours, taken for 28 days
  • PrEP: Pre-exposure prophylaxis for high-risk individuals — daily tenofovir/emtricitabine

blocks.heading: NORMAL FUNCTION
blocks.html:
• Intact CD4 count >500
  • Functional cell-mediated and humoral immunity
  • No opportunistic infections
  • Normal immune surveillance for malignancies

blocks.heading: DYSFUNCTION
blocks.html:
• HIV binds to CD4 cells, enters, replicates
  • CD4 cell destruction → progressive immunodeficiency
  • CD4 <200: AIDS — severe OI risk
  • Chronic inflammation → accelerated aging, cardiovascular disease

blocks.heading: ⚠ Risk Factors (Non-Modifiable)
blocks.html:
• Vertical transmission (mother to child)
  • Blood transfusion (rare in screened blood)
  • Occupational exposure (needlestick 0.3% risk)

blocks.heading: 💡 Risk Factors (Modifiable)
blocks.html:
• Unprotected sexual intercourse (anal > vaginal > oral)
  • Sharing needles/injection equipment
  • Multiple sexual partners
  • Sexually transmitted infections (increases transmission risk)
  • Men who have sex with men (highest prevalence group in Caribbean)

blocks.heading: 🔥 Complications
blocks.html: Opportunistic infections: PCP, TB, cryptococcal meningitis, toxoplasmosis • Malignancies: Kaposi sarcoma, lymphoma, cervical cancer • HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder (HAND) • Wasting syndrome • Cardiovascular, renal, hepatic disease (chronic inflammation) • Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS)
NRG Opposite: CD4 cells destroyed → immune system collapses → opportunistic infections and malignancies

1. HIV gp120 binds CD4 + CCR5/CXCR4 receptor

2. Viral RNA enters cell → reverse transcriptase → DNA

3. Viral DNA integrates into host genome (latency possible)

4. New virions bud from cell → cell death

5. CD4 count falls progressively

6. Immunodeficiency allows opportunistic infections

blocks.heading: Key Detail
blocks.html: HIV is a retrovirus with reverse transcriptase enzyme. It integrates into host DNA, making eradication nearly impossible. The latent reservoir (resting CD4 cells) is why ART must be lifelong. Drug classes target different stages: NRTIs/NNRTIs (reverse transcriptase), PIs (protease), INSTIs (integrase).

blocks.heading: Clinical Result
blocks.html: Untreated HIV progresses through stages: acute seroconversion (flu-like illness), clinical latency (asymptomatic, CD4 declining), symptomatic (CD4 200-350, recurrent infections), AIDS (CD4 <200 or AIDS-defining illness). With ART, life expectancy approaches normal.
NRG Sequencing: Each step leads to the next — understand the cascade to predict S/S and management

blocks.heading: Early / Mild
blocks.html:
• Acute seroconversion: fever, pharyngitis, rash, lymphadenopathy (2-4 weeks post-exposure)
  • Clinical latency: often asymptomatic for years

blocks.heading: Severe
blocks.html:
• Recurrent infections (oral candidiasis, shingles)
  • Chronic diarrhea, weight loss
  • Night sweats, persistent fever
  • Lymphadenopathy
  • Oral hairy leukoplakia

blocks.heading: PCP pneumonia: severe dyspnea, hypoxemia, diffuse infiltrates
blocks.html:
• PCP pneumonia: severe dyspnea, hypoxemia, diffuse infiltrates
  • Cryptococcal meningitis: headache, fever, altered LOC
  • Toxoplasma encephalitis: seizures, focal deficits
  • TB (most common OI globally)
  • THIS IS A MEDICAL EMERGENCY

blocks.heading: Diagnostic / Assessment Findings
blocks.html:
• 4th gen HIV Ag/Ab test: screening
  • HIV viral load: quantifies RNA copies
  • CD4 count: stage and guide OI prophylaxis
  • Resistance testing: guides ART selection
  • CBC: anemia, thrombocytopenia common
  • CMP: renal/hepatic function for ART dosing

blocks.heading: Link Patho to S/S
blocks.html:
CD4 decline → Recurrent infections, fatigue

Immunosuppression → Opportunistic infections vary by CD4 level

Chronic inflammation → Cardiovascular disease, neurocognitive decline

Malabsorption → Chronic diarrhea, weight loss, wasting

blocks.heading: Cardiovascular
blocks.html:
• BP, HR
  • Signs of dehydration (diarrhea)
  • Peripheral edema (nephrotic syndrome, malnutrition)

blocks.heading: Respiratory
blocks.html:
• Respiratory rate, SpO2 (PCP, TB)
  • Cough, sputum
  • Lung sounds

blocks.heading: Neurological
blocks.html:
• Mental status (cryptococcal meningitis, HAND)
  • Focal neurological deficits (toxoplasmosis, PML)
  • Headache severity

blocks.heading: Key Laboratory & Diagnostic Tests
rows: Detects p24 Ag + Ab; window 2-4 weeks
Stages disease; <200 = AIDS; guides OI prophylaxis

blocks.heading: Priority Actions
blocks.html: STRICT CONFIDENTIALITY — HIV status is protected health information. Never disclose without patient consent. Assess for opportunistic infections based on CD4 count. Screen for TB (most common OI). Evaluate medication adherence (lifelong ART).

blocks.heading: 💊 Pharmacology - Nursing Monitoring
rows: Must start within 72 hours, take for 28 days

blocks.heading: Confidentiality & ART Adherence Alert
blocks.html: HIV status is CONFIDENTIAL — protected by law. Disclosure without consent is illegal (except mandatory reporting to public health, partner notification programs). ART must be taken EVERY DAY for LIFE. Missing doses leads to resistance. U=U: Undetectable viral load = cannot transmit sexually.

blocks.heading: Lifestyle & Patient Education
blocks.html:
• DAILY lifelong ART adherence — use pillboxes, alarms, routines
  • U=U counseling — undetectable = untransmittable
  • Safe sex practices (condoms, PrEP for partners)
  • Regular STI screening
  • Nutritional support — balanced diet, food safety (CD4 <200: avoid raw foods)
🚨 Report Immediately: CD4 <200 | New opportunistic infection | Severe headache with fever | Confusion | Severe dyspnea | Adverse drug reaction (rash, jaundice)

blocks.heading: Nursing Diagnosis
blocks.html: Risk for infection related to immunodeficiency (CD4 180) as evidenced by history of oral candidiasis, recurrent respiratory infections, and CD4 count below 200

blocks.heading: Goal / Outcome
blocks.html: Patient will remain free of opportunistic infections and achieve undetectable viral load within 6 months of ART initiation.

blocks.heading: Interventions
blocks.html:
• Initiate ART per protocol
  • Start PCP prophylaxis (TMP-SMX) — CD4 <200
  • Screen for TB and treat if positive
  • Monitor CD4 and viral load regularly
  • Educate on strict medication adherence
  • Provide psychosocial support and counseling

blocks.heading: Rationale
blocks.html: ART restores immune function and prevents OIs. PCP prophylaxis prevents the most common AIDS-defining pneumonia. TB screening is essential — TB is the leading cause of death in HIV globally. Adherence prevents resistance and treatment failure.

blocks.heading: Evaluation
blocks.html: Viral load undetectable at 3 months. CD4 increased to 280. No new OIs. Patient reports 100% adherence. Understanding of U=U and safe sex practices.
NRG Care Plan Formula: Problem → Goal → Interventions → Rationale → Evaluation

What system is being tested?

Immune — CD4 cell destruction and opportunistic infections

What is the priority?

ART adherence + OI prophylaxis (CD4 <200) + strict confidentiality

What is unsafe?

Disclosing HIV status without consent, missing ART doses, not screening for TB

What restores function?

Daily ART suppresses viral replication, restores CD4, prevents OIs

blocks.heading: 💡 Key Memory Aids for RENR
blocks.html:
• U=U: Undetectable = Untransmittable — patient with VL <50 cannot sexually transmit HIV
  • CD4 <200: AIDS threshold — start PCP prophylaxis (TMP-SMX)
  • PEP 72 hours: Must start within 72 hours of exposure, continue 28 days
  • Confidentiality: HIV status is protected by law — never disclose without consent
  • TB screening: ALL HIV patients must be screened for TB — leading cause of HIV death globally
NRG System Focus Formula: HIV → Immune → CD4 destruction → Immunodeficiency → Priority: ART adherence + OI prophylaxis + Confidentiality

question.stem: A nurse is caring for a patient newly diagnosed with HIV (CD4 150, viral load 85,000 copies/mL). The patient's spouse arrives and asks the nurse what is wrong with their partner. The patient has not disclosed their HIV status to anyone. What is the nurse's best response?

options.html: Tell the spouse that the patient has HIV because marital partners have a right to know
Inform the spouse that the patient has a respiratory infection that requires treatment
Tell the spouse that the patient's medical information is confidential and they need to speak with the patient directly
Contact the physician to obtain permission to disclose the HIV status to the spouse

question.rationale: Patient confidentiality is an absolute ethical and legal obligation. The patient has decisional capacity and the right to disclose (or not disclose) their own health information. The nurse must direct the spouse to speak with the patient. Disclosing without consent (Option A) violates patient autonomy, trust, and potentially the law. Option B is deceptive and dishonest. Option D is inappropriate — a physician cannot override a competent patient's right to confidentiality.

why.html: Breach of confidentiality — patient has right to self-disclose
Physician cannot override competent patient's confidentiality
